newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: LME copper stocks seen up 2,000-5,000 tonnes - trade.
newsitem.headline: LME copper stocks seen up 2,000-5,000 tonnes - trade.

text.p: Far East metal traders said on Friday that they expected London Metal Exchange (LME) copper stocks to rise by between 2,000-5,000 tonnes later in the day.
Most dealers here believe LME aluminium stocks will probably post a fall of 1,000 to 2,000 tonnes.
"We think copper is going to move up by 4,000 to 5,000 tonnes," the general manager of one metal dealing company said.
"Four thousand to 5,000 should be just right," a dealer for a Japanese metal trading firm added.
Vinod Kumar, director of Singapore-based metal firm Donald Mcarthy, said he would opt for a more modest increase in the LME stocks report, which is due out at 0900 GMT.
"Today, I think copper will go up 2,000 to 3,000 tonnes," he said.
Traders said small amounts of copper continue to arrive in Singapore warehouses with most material coming from China.
One dealer said about 2,000 tonnes arrived in the city-state this week while another 3,000 tonnes will probably come in by the following week.
Several thousand tonnes have not been placed on warrant with the LME's Singapore warehouse. One trader estimated the amount at about 20,000 tonnes.
"It's quite a lot," Kumar said when asked how much of the copper remains off-warrant in warehouses here.
The amount of copper in the LME warehouse here reached 16,475 tonnes in last Tuesday's LME report, up 2,350 tonnes from the previous Friday's report.
Three month copper prices were quoted by dealers here at around US$2,140/45 a tonne at 0330 GMT against the $2,148 a tonne seen in late trade in London on Thursday.
Aluminium prices were quoted at about $1,531/36 a tonne at 0330 GMT compared with late trade in London yesterday of $1,528 a tonne, traders said.
